tq.quote: The powerful yet lightweight Shimano EP6 mid-drive motor delivers reliable performance and smooth, natural assistance. With a full 85 Nm of torque, it's easier to start on steeper roads or when fully loaded even when pedaling at lower cadences.

The powerful Shimano EP6 motor has been customized for urban riding, with up to 85Nm of torque at low cadence for easy starts and quick inclines. A 420Wh battery is secured inside the downtube for protection from weather, bumps, and theft, and an additional 252Wh battery can be purchased to extend your range for longer commutes or all kinds of adventures.

fold.quote: An ingenious mechanism allows you to quickly rotate the handlebars 90 degrees, and the pedals fold flat too if parking space is at a premium.
fold.basis: handlebar rotates and pedals fold; frame does not fold

notes: Uses the Carpe 10 20mph build (src link). Orbea's US configurator gives no class, speed spec, range, weight or max load. eBikes International's Carpe 10 test report (not speed-specific) confirms 85Nm and 420Wh; its 'SRP is $5,899' is likely a non-US price, so not used. 99 Spokes lists the same price and specs as Orbea. Space-saving stem and folding pedals, but the frame does not fold. Recheck: maker product and catalog pages (incl. hidden text) give no class word, only the '20mph' build name; Around the Cycle (US dealer) lists only Carpe 28mph builds (Class 3).
